statement: A contest question has five choices, is worth 4 points, and a wrong answer costs nothing. Kai will guess on his last 12 questions. On 4 he can rule out three wrong choices, on 3 he can rule out two, and on the other 5 nothing. On average, how many points do these 12 guesses earn him?

choices.misconception: I thought a random guess earns nothing on average, so I counted no points from any of the twelve.
I found how many of the twelve he gets right on average, 4, and gave that instead of the points.
I used a one-in-five chance for every guess, ignoring the choices he had ruled out.
I left out the five questions where he can rule out nothing, thinking a blind guess is not worth anything.

hints: How many choices are left on each kind of question?
With no penalty, every guess has an average value: the chance it is right times the points it is worth. Find the average number of correct guesses in each group, add them, then turn that into points.
Two choices are left on 4 questions, three on 3 questions and five on 5 questions. On average that is 4 x 1/2 + 3 x 1/3 + 5 x 1/5 correct guesses.

solutions.reliable: On the 4 questions with two choices left, each guess is right with probability 1/2, so on average 2 are right. On the 3 questions with three choices left, each is right with probability 1/3, so on average 1 is right. On the 5 blind guesses, each is right with probability 1/5, so on average 1 is right. That is 2 + 1 + 1 = 4 correct answers on average, worth 4 x 4 = 16 points. The transferable idea: with no penalty, every guess has positive value, even a blind one, and each eliminated choice raises it.
solutions.elegant: In each group, the expected number of correct guesses is the number of questions divided by the number of choices left: 4/2 + 3/3 + 5/5 = 2 + 1 + 1 = 4, so 16 points. Even the five blind guesses add 4 points on average.

whyOnTest: No-penalty scoring means every question gets an answer, and this checks whether a student can turn eliminations, and blind guesses, into an expected score.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
